label: A115, SQF Mogilev to ALQ via DQH Berlin, 16 June 1942

why: This is Bletchley Park's own typed German decrypt, quoted in the notes (not our decipherment); four sentences, fully clear. The repository does not contain our own decipherment of the Orpo message.

label: R1874, Alvise Mocenigo, Madrid, 26 Oct 1628 (the contemporary decipherment)
sample_original: il conte di olivares ha desiderato con buone parole et promesse condurlo a risolutione di ritornar in fiandra anco con qualche violente termine lo ha procurato
sample_en: Count Olivares wished with kind words and promises to bring him to resolve to return to Flanders, and has even tried it with some violent terms.
why: Italian despatch paragraphs with expanded abbreviations; fluent and fully coherent, but unpunctuated, lowercase, with paragraphs as single run-on blocks, and a trailing '...' truncation; it needs punctuation and a translation, not cryptanalysis. The text is the contemporary decipherment transcribed by us, not our own solution.

label: Harley MS 260 f. 419r-v, 29 Jan 1573
sample_original: hee spake with Glascoe <3> and Davison with him, I see there was a greate mistakinge of our doinges
sample_en: (already English) he spoke with Glasgow and Davison with him; I see there was a great mistaking of our doings.
why: Clear English letter-book text with the cipher words inline as <n> tags; the cipher words are code names (Alencon, the Queen) glossed by Adam Wright, so the narrative is coherent once the tags are resolved; one tag <^ 4 d H m 11 11 I J> and one place name {Valery} remain unread. Needs normalising of the tags.

label: BnF fr. 15572 f. 43, 30 Jan 1586
sample_original: La dicte dame m'a elle mesme baillé les lettres en mes mains : n'estoient que de generale recommendation ; et ces lors je jugeai qui [qu'il] pratiquoit ici quelque chose
sample_en: The said lady herself put the letters into my hands: they were only general recommendations; and from then on I judged that he was plotting something here.
why: George Lasry's edited French in three punctuated paragraphs, only about six [?] marks; the syntax is sometimes odd ('qui' for 'que') and the passage uses figurative names (concierge, jardinier, tailleurs de pierre) that make the sense obscure, but the sentences build and translate.

label: No. 17 (R4805), Bartolomeo Tantucci to Antonio del Vescovo, 25 Aug 1528
sample_original: Parlo breve et in substantia perché la cifra vuol così.
sample_en: I speak briefly and in substance because the cipher requires it.
why: Lasry's edited Italian with expanded abbreviations; a handful of (?) and [?] marks (about 7 in 11 lines, a few garbled words such as 'lco[??]stren[?]niare'), roughly 85% solved, yet the three numbered points are readable sentences. Line breaks follow the PDF.

label: R9487, 13 Dec 1527: the Claro, f. 34r
sample_original: Todos los enemigos se retirayeron de cabe Milan, de suerte que ahora es señor de la campaña Antonio de Leyva y corre por do quiere
sample_en: All the enemies withdrew from near Milan, so that Antonio de Leyva is now master of the countryside and runs wherever he wishes.
why: Contemporary decipherment ('Claro'), diplomatic transcription. Section A and the closing paragraph build sentences, but the leaf is torn: B and the start of C are half-lines ending in '[…]' and mostly cannot be assembled ('es de maravillar de qualquier desor[den …]'). Roughly half of the page reads.

label: R1057, Berlin, 4 Feb 1792, Van Reede to William V
sample_original: Il voudra bien en prévenir Monseigneur le Prince d'Orange et avoir la bonté de lui remettre ma lettre
sample_en: He will kindly inform His Highness the Prince of Orange and be so good as to hand him my letter.
why: Three sentences of French with hyphenated syllable breaks and one word uncertain (se[r?]…); an English translation is given. Short; the trailing figures are declared nulls.

label: R1408, HHStA Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 14 Fasc. 20, Warsaw, 24 Dec 1627
sample_original: Mi ricordo che, fra li altri honori che [120] mi f(f)ece in Nicolspurg, mi confido d'hauer dato intentione a questa Se(e)renissima [100] [113] de uoler conferire un canonicato d'Olmiz ad uno de li [123] suoi figli
sample_en: I remember that, among the other honours that [you] did me at Nikolsburg, I trust I gave this Most Serene [Queen] the expectation of conferring a canonry of Olomouc on one of her sons.
why: One short Italian letter: the raw decode is unspaced, the word-divided version has about 13 unread code groups ([120], [154] x3, [160] x3, [100] [113], [123], [151], [157], [223] [159]) and the filled-in version is explicitly inference, not reading. The skeleton is clear and translatable, but the object of the request is missing, so holes fall in most clauses.
